purpose: Sodium fluoride rinse is used to help prevent tooth decay and cavities. It strengthens your tooth enamel to make your teeth more resistant to acid and bacteria. Your dentist or doctor may recommend it if you are at higher risk for cavities or have sensitive teeth.
how_it_works: Fluoride is a natural mineral that gets absorbed into the outer layer of your teeth, called enamel, making it harder and stronger. It helps repair early damage to your teeth before it turns into a full cavity. It also makes it harder for the bacteria in your mouth to produce the acids that cause tooth decay.
common_side_effects: This rinse is generally very well tolerated. Some people may notice a mild temporary taste change or slight tooth sensitivity. If you accidentally swallow large amounts regularly, it could cause nausea or stomach upset, which is why it is important to spit it out after rinsing.
warnings: Do not swallow this rinse — always spit it out after use. Keep it out of reach of children under 6 years old, as they may accidentally swallow it. Too much fluoride over time can cause white spots on teeth, especially in young children. Tell your dentist or doctor about all other fluoride products you use, including toothpaste, to avoid getting too much fluoride.
typical_dosing: Most adults and children over 6 years old use this rinse once daily, usually at bedtime after brushing your teeth. Swish about 10 mL (2 teaspoons) around your mouth for 1 minute, then spit it all out. Do not eat, drink, or rinse your mouth with water for at least 30 minutes afterward to let the fluoride work properly.
